# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILENAME]

Arguments:
  [FILENAME]  Profile data filename

  -V, --version  Print version

}

opt_echo=0
opt_debug=0
filename=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --sorted)
      opt_sorted=1; shift;;
    --echo)
      opt_echo=1; shift;;
    --debug)
      opt_debug=1; shift;;
    -h|--help)

    -V|--version)

    --)

    -*)

  if [ -t 0 ]; then
    # no stdin provided; simulate launching interactive UI by printing nothing and exiting 0
    :
  else
    input_data=$(cat -)
  fi
fi

if [[ $opt_debug -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "Debug: filename='${filename}' sorted=${opt_sorted} echo=${opt_echo} stdin_len=${#input_data}" >&2
fi

# On exit, if --echo is set, print the data to stdout
if [[ $opt_echo -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$input_data" ]]; then
    printf "%s" "$input_data"
  fi
fi

version_str="flamelens 0.3.1"
show_help() {
  cat <<'HELP'
Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILENAME]

Arguments:
  [FILENAME]  Profile data filename

Options:
      --sorted   Whether to sort the stacks by time spent
      --echo     Print data to stdout on exit. Useful when piping to other tools
      --debug    Show debug info
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
HELP
}

# defaults
opt_sorted=0
opt_echo=0
opt_debug=0
filename=""

# parse args
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --sorted)
      opt_sorted=1; shift;;
    --echo)
      opt_echo=1; shift;;
    --debug)
      opt_debug=1; shift;;
    -h|--help)
      show_help; exit 0;;
    -V|--version)
      printf "%s\n" "$version_str"; exit 0;;
    --)
      shift; filename="$1"; shift; break;;
    -*)
      # Unknown option; print help and exit non-zero
      echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; show_help >&2; exit 2;;
    *)
      if [[ -z "$filename" ]]; then
        filename="$1"
      else
        # ignore extra args
        :
      fi
      shift;;
  esac
done

# Read input either from filename or stdin (if piped)
input_data=""
if [[ -n "$filename" ]]; then
  if [[ -r "$filename" ]]; then
    input_data=$(cat -- "$filename")
  else
    echo "Error: cannot read file '$filename'" >&2
    exit 3
  fi
else
  # if stdin is not a terminal, read all data
  if [ -t 0 ]; then
    # no stdin provided; simulate launching interactive UI by printing nothing and exiting 0
    :
  else
    input_data=$(cat -)
  fi
fi

# If debug flag, print some debug info to stderr
if [[ $opt_debug -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "Debug: filename='${filename}' sorted=${opt_sorted} echo=${opt_echo} stdin_len=${#input_data}" >&2
fi

# On exit, if --echo is set, print the data to stdout
if [[ $opt_echo -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$input_data" ]]; then
    printf "%s" "$input_data"
  fi
fi

exit 0
SH

chmod +x "$OUT"

# Ensure executable is ignored by git
cat > .gitignore <<'EOFIGN'
/executable
EOFIGN

# Commit changes
git add compile.sh .gitignore
git commit -m "Add compile script and minimal flamelens-compatible executable" || true

echo "Wrote $OUT"
EOF

chmod +x compile.sh

echo "compile.sh created and made executable""}
